policy: Editorial links to bounded draft lessons, not certification of complete subject or book coverage. Source evidence statuses are preserved independently.

Finite weighted average; separate from a promised individual outcome or estimator theory.

Finite sample-mean and normal-model interval/power examples prepare for sampling theory. Summary statistics and planning assumptions are entered rather than sampled; general sample generation, central-limit theorems and distributional diagnostics remain separate.
A descriptive contrast compares fixed group means; independent and paired sampling tests are not implemented.

Exact binomial, known/estimated-spread normal-mean intervals and an iid-normal variance interval are distinct fixed-coverage procedures. Mean and variance endpoints have different physical units; none is a posterior probability for a fixed unknown parameter.

Bounded binomial, randomization, sign/rank and F procedures state separate hypotheses and exact or model-based references. Signed ranks require the declared symmetric paired-null signs; Mann–Whitney uses exchangeable equal-distribution labels and is not an unrestricted median test. P-values are not probabilities of the null.

Bounded sign, paired signed-rank and independent-group Mann–Whitney references enumerate their complete conditional null assignments. Finite references enumerate all balanced raw-mean or pooled-rank label assignments under their stated nulls. The observed examples are constructions, with ties handled directly; no Monte Carlo sampler or general assignment engine is implemented.

Three constructed readings per group and a separate known-spread two-group power model illustrate the roles of independent replication. The power model enters n per group, distinguishes total 2n, and assumes a true planning effect. Broader design, pseudoreplication diagnostics, empirical data generation and unknown-spread power remain separate.

A small constructed complete-block comparison follows within-block differences while common block offsets cancel. This descriptive contrast does not supply an ANOVA, randomization distribution or empirical treatment-effect claim.

A balanced three-group, nine-reading construction decomposes total variation into between/within sums of squares, divides by 2/6 degrees of freedom and compares their mean squares. The F(2,6) tail uses an explicitly stated independent-normal/common-variance model; general designs and pairwise procedures remain separate.
